For protein-coding genes only (gene_biotype == 'protein_coding', exact match; 19,942 genes), with gene expression summarized as the mean of the batch-corrected read counts across the 723 samples and gene lengths taken from the Length column as-is (bp), the Pearson correlation coefficient between gene length and gene expression is r = 0.320356 (primary definition: Length vs log2(mean expression + 1); scipy.stats.pearsonr, p < 1e-300). 

Sensitivity variants: (a) Length vs raw mean expression: r = 0.050383; (b) log10(Length) vs log2(mean+1): r = 0.421946; (c) Length vs mean of per-sample log2(count+1): r = 0.314239; (median summary) r = 0.311804; dropping the 645 zero-mean genes r = 0.293425. All 19,942 protein-coding genes retained in the primary analysis (zero-mean genes mapped to log2(1)=0). Final answer (primary): r = 0.320356 (≈ 0.3204).
